ShiroFOC closes motor-control loops locally and communicates with a coordinating motherboard over CAN. This presentation follows the current connected KiCad redraw. It explains the released circuit, documented calculations and engineering tradeoffs. The schematic is ready for first-prototype PCB layout. It is not a fabrication release or a hardware qualification. Current and thermal values remain design targets.

The design constraints specify 25 Arms free-air, 40 Arms with a defined heatsink or forced airflow, and 80 A peak for no more than two seconds. These refer to motor phase current. They are not demonstrated ratings. An 80 A instantaneous peak cannot be commissioned while a +60 A comparator trip is active. Field-oriented control transforms measured phase currents into a rotor-related coordinate system. Current regulators control torque-producing and field-related components, then modulation generates complementary PWM. The position sensor provides the rotor-angle reference. Integration reduces component count and pin-level interconnects, while external MOSFETs allow package and loss selection. This is an explanation of the intended control architecture, not a claim that firmware already implements it. Sources: DESIGN_CONSTRAINTS.md, Fixed architecture, and FIRMWARE_BRINGUP_CONTRACT.md.

The external logic rail supplies the embedded MCU, sensor interfaces, CAN and service bridge. The gate-driver rail depends on VM, so USB-only operation cannot drive the inverter or brake. Both input supplies may be attached because the mux provides reverse-current blocking. On VM loss, firmware invalidates motor state and clears torque commands. On return it repeats the driver setup rather than continuing from a stale command. Source: DESIGN_CONSTRAINTS.md, Auxiliary power architecture, and FIRMWARE_BRINGUP_CONTRACT.md, Runtime rules.

One time constant leaves roughly 37 percent of the starting voltage, so the board is not discharged after 16 minutes merely because that is the time constant. When OUTx is low, the internal bootstrap diode charges the capacitor from VCC. When the high-side MOSFET turns on, OUTx rises and the capacitor keeps the high-side driver supply above that moving source. The capacitor voltage rating concerns the BOOT-to-OUT differential, while physical spacing also sees switch-node common-mode motion. The 56 nC charge figure is conservative at the TI datasheet test conditions but does not include all high-side supply consumption. A 100 kΩ gate-source resistor draws about 100 µA at 10 V, adding 5 nC over a 50 µs dwell, equivalent to 0.05 V on 100 nF.
